title: Review: entire project — my-oss pass
notes:
Maintainer risk: MEDIUM — Two P0 bugs: expired EC384 test cert and missing KARI decrypt oracle test. Three P1 issues: wrong error variant for boundary failure, library panic on OS RNG (documented limitation of rsa crate), pub-vs-pub(crate) visibility. No CVEs, no data loss paths, no panics in normal operation.
Confidence: 85% chance of no missed bugs. Least confident: KARI decrypt path — only tested from encrypt-side (our code → OpenSSL), never from decrypt-side (OpenSSL → our code). The agree_ecdh trait contract and KDF parameters are correct in isolation but the round-trip is not independently validated. Uncertainty driven by: not running OpenSSL as the encryptor for KARI. Would raise confidence if: an OpenSSL-encrypted KARI fixture + our own DecryptionKey::agree_ecdh implementation test existed.
Idiom rating: ACCEPTABLE — No unsafe, no Box<dyn Error> in API, no gratuitous clones, all expect() have justification comments. Missing Display on three key types, SmimeError::Other overused for 8+ failure modes, BodyStructure pub vs pub(crate). Nothing that would make a Rust practitioner wince at the structural level.
Rust idiom confidence: 90% chance of no missed issue. Least confident: SmimeError::Other subcategories — there may be more distinct failure modes that deserve structured variants that I missed. Uncertainty driven by: not checking every call site for Other(). Would raise confidence if: running clippy::pedantic and addressing all lints.
